title: Muskyttehool (Flatlands)
summary: Muskyttehool is a Flatlands, Kings County placename for a pool or wet place where rushes grew. The popular Musquito hole explanation is best understood as a misunderstanding of a rush-place name.
map_geometry_source: approximate modern Flatlands, Brooklyn marker; not an exact historic pool or boundary
introduction_content: Muskyttehool names a locality at Flatlands in Brooklyn. The name is explained as a hybrid form: an Algonquian rush-place word joined to the English word hole.
history_content: Flatlands locality and the rush-place interpretation are brought together here. The source context here is interpretive rather than a separate time-specific occurrence.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as a pool of water where rushes grow. Musquito hole is treated as a later popular misunderstanding rather than the source of the name. The history cross-references Mosquetah and Musquatax for related rush-place forms.

Why Place Names Matter

“Mapping, in this context, is not about naming for ownership, it is about recognising and respecting these life forces as kin.”

— Native Land Digital, Indigenous Place Names (2024), Indigenous Mapping is Relational section

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: The point is an approximate general marker in Flatlands, Brooklyn. It represents a broad locality, not an exact pool, marsh, or historical boundary.
